prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE stream reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client transport permanently fails (max attempts exhausted, or an unrecoverable error during a reconnection attempt), the failure was not surfaced to the code awaiting the original request's response — the caller was left hanging indefinitely instead of receiving an error. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE stream reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client transport permanently fails (max attempts exhausted, or an unrecoverable error during a reconnection attempt), the failure was not surfaced to the code awaiting the original request's response — the caller was left hanging indefinitely instead of receiving an error. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 fixes the failure at its source in `_handle_reconnection`: when MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS is exceeded it builds a proper JSONRPCError keyed to the original request's id and sends it on `read_stream_writer`, but only for `JSONRPCRequest` messages (guarded by an `isinstance` check), so notifications aren't incorrectly errored and only the specific stalled request is affected. It also converts a `# pragma: no cover` branch into one with real log output, indicating the path is now exercised by tests. #3098 instead adds a general-purpose `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig a `StreamableHTTPError` out of anyio `BaseExceptionGroup` nesting and changes `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` to a plain import — a broader, connection-level approach (raising out through the TaskGroup) that tears down the whole session rather than isolating the failure to the affected request, and the diff shown doesn't include a call site that actually raises/uses the unwrapped `StreamableHTTPError`, making its fix harder to verify as complete from the diff alone.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser split/matched auth-param values using naive substring/comma logic that breaks when quoted parameter values themselves contain commas (or when a parameter name is a substring of another, e.g. 'error' vs 'error_description'). Both add a near-identical quote-aware, escape-aware comma-splitting helper to correctly tokenize the header into individual auth-param entries before matching. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser split/matched auth-param values using naive substring/comma logic that breaks when quoted parameter values themselves contain commas (or when a parameter name is a substring of another, e.g. 'error' vs 'error_description'). Both add a near-identical quote-aware, escape-aware comma-splitting helper to correctly tokenize the header into individual auth-param entries before matching. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add functionally equivalent quote/escape-aware comma splitters at the same location in utils.py, so they resolve the identical root cause. #3041's implementation additionally introduces _extract_bearer_auth_params, which explicitly partitions each top-level segment into scheme and remainder and filters for the 'bearer' scheme before collecting params — this correctly handles a WWW-Authenticate header containing multiple challenges (e.g. Basic + Bearer separated by a top-level comma per RFC 7235). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of params, which does not disambiguate a second scheme token if the header contains more than one challenge. This is a visible structural difference in the pasted diffs, not a style preference.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py attempts json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, so for union types like `str | None` a plain string that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "[1,2]") gets silently parsed into the wrong Python value instead of being kept as a string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py attempts json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, so for union types like `str | None` a plain string that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "[1,2]") gets silently parsed into the wrong Python value instead of being kept as a string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056's _is_optional_str only suppresses pre-parsing for the specific str|None shape where no other union member could ever be a valid JSON-decode target, and it unwraps Annotated (e.g. Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None) before comparing. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead skips parsing for ANY union whose members are all in a fixed {str,int,float,bool,NoneType} set — it does not unwrap Annotated, so it fails to short-circuit for the common Annotated[str, Field(...)] pattern, and it also disables the previously-working numeric-string coercion for unions like str|int and str|bool, which is a behavior change beyond the reported bug.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart (or any fresh OAuthClientProvider that only reloads tokens/client_info from storage), OAuthContext.oauth_metadata is empty, so the client doesn't know the authorization server's token endpoint and a cold-start token refresh breaks or is forced into full rediscovery/re-auth. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart (or any fresh OAuthClientProvider that only reloads tokens/client_info from storage), OAuthContext.oauth_metadata is empty, so the client doesn't know the authorization server's token endpoint and a cold-start token refresh breaks or is forced into full rediscovery/re-auth. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3263 fixes this without changing the public TokenStorage Protocol: it re-runs AS metadata discovery in-memory before a cold-start refresh and adds an issuer-binding check to validate the rediscovered metadata, plus an eager_discovery_attempted flag so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every refresh. #2492 instead adds new get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata methods to the TokenStorage Protocol (an interface change every storage implementation must opt into to benefit) and trusts whatever metadata was cached at storage time with no freshness/issuer validation on reload.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the failure at its source in `_handle_reconnection`: when MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS is exceeded it builds a proper JSONRPCError keyed to the original request's id and sends it on `read_stream_writer`, but only for `JSONRPCRequest` messages (guarded by an `isinstance` check), so notifications aren't incorrectly errored and only the specific stalled request is affected. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add functionally equivalent quote/escape-aware comma splitters at the same location in utils.py, so they resolve the identical root cause. #3041's implementation additionally introduces _extract_bearer_auth_params, which explicitly partitions each top-level segment into scheme and remainder and filters for the 'bearer' scheme before collecting params — this correctly handles a WWW-Authenticate header containing multiple challenges (e.g. Basic + Bearer separated by a top-level comma per RFC 7235). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of params, which does not disambiguate a second scheme token if the header contains more than one challenge. This is a visible structural difference in the pasted diffs, not a style preference.
